rationale: P characterises whether required braking occurs—the system behaviour directly evaluated by T and explicitly established by SG-1 and FR-7. H-1 supports the declared operational conditions and collision context. The braking response is therefore part of the phenomenon, not merely a mechanism affecting its evaluation. P does not incorporate sensing, communication, internal computation, or mechanism-specific timing constraints.
determining_elements: “Whether the vehicle executes a braking maneuver when braking is required” directly addresses occurrence versus omission of the action required by T.
The collision-avoidance condition involving a road user or static obstacle is supported by H-1 and FR-7.
The straight-ahead, single-lane-road scenario at 50 km/h in good weather, with a pedestrian crossing 20 m ahead, matches H-1's operational situation.
The scope's “decide and perform braking” describes the required functional response without separately including decision algorithms or other implementation mechanisms.
